chapter: A musical family and the old New Orleans bands
title: Jim Robinson and Slow Drag, overrated by the revivalists
summary: Danny says Jim Robinson's trombone pattern is repeated each chorus and the revival cult reveres him and bassist Slow Drag too much.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: You mentioned Jim Robinson, a trombonist. Who was he?

Jim Robinson was a trombone player who became...supposed to have been the greatest New Orleans trombone player after Kid Ory. Now, he was in that band. He was probably out to ...(?)... that band. But the Australian trombone players, they all got something from Jim Robinson -- which is the same pattern he plays in every chorus. [SINGS TWO BAR REFRAIN] He played the bass trombone.

So you know, if he was playing something in the first register, that to people is way out. That don't mean nothin' to these people. So when you're playing in the first position, like Jimmy Harrison or Higgenbotham playing up there, using all different (?).
